actions: set bit in qualifying_orderkeys bitset (indexed by o_orderkey)
store o_orderpriority code in priority_by_orderkey array (indexed by o_orderkey)

operators.note: Q4 is not part of scan_lineitem_full consumer set; must scan independently

operators.description: For each lineitem row: if qualifying_orderkeys[l_orderkey] is set AND l_commitdate < l_receiptdate, set found_orderkeys[l_orderkey]
Iterate qualifying_orderkeys bitset; for each set bit k, if found_orderkeys[k] is set, increment counts[priority_by_orderkey[k]]
operators.data_structure: int64[5] counters indexed by dict code

operators.note: Map dict codes back to strings, sort 5 rows alphabetically by priority string. Output order: 1-URGENT, 2-HIGH, 3-MEDIUM, 4-NOT SPECIFIED, 5-LOW

qualifying_orderkeys.description: Indexed by o_orderkey; marks orders passing date filter

found_orderkeys.description: Indexed by o_orderkey; marks orders with qualifying lineitem

priority_by_orderkey.description: Maps orderkey -> orderpriority dict code for date-filtered orders

agg_counters.description: One counter per orderpriority dict code

step_1.note: scan_orders_full delivers rows via callback; date filter + bitset/array writes are thread-safe via per-thread local bitsets merged at end

step_2_3.note: Lineitem scan is the bottleneck (720MB from HDD). Parallel morsels with thread-local found_orderkeys bitsets, merged via OR at end. Each thread: read morsel, check qualifying bitset, check commitdate < receiptdate, set found bitset.

step_4.note: Iterate qualifying bitset (~540K set bits), check found bitset, increment 5 counters. Trivial cost.

indexes.purpose: skip_blocks during date filter in step 1 (if shared scan supports block skipping)

notes: Q4 is NOT in the scan_lineitem_full consumer set, so the tail performs its own lineitem scan of 3 columns (720MB). The semi-join uses dual bitsets (qualifying + found, 7.2MB each, both fit in L3 cache) for cache-friendly probing. The priority_by_orderkey array (57MB) exceeds L3 but is written/read sparsely. Aggregation is trivially 5 direct counters.
